arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Thu: she phoned at 10:23, 'can it wait until Saturday night, at the cinema?'; at 14:00 she came up for leftover Leblebi Soup. Fri: tomorrow fixed, 18:30 at Avi's, a walk, the 21:00 horror film; 'before the film, or after'; the 04 number again, face down. Next: first date Sat Nov 21, she almost tells him; midpoint Wed Nov 25, Lior lets it slip.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Thu: Ruti's email (jobs without an agency); 'can I think about it?' saved as a draft; Gadi: 'late is a kind of on time, Sunday, promise'; Ishai sent the coffee-shop logo package Thu night. Fri: a 'tiny thing for Ruti's dreidel' on Shabbat; Ishai answers 'Sunday. Nothing else.' Next: Sunday's number; Ruti still unanswered.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Thu: came at 16:00 with a duffel ('the kitchen floor is a lake'), then on the phone 'somewhere very quiet' said 'amazing' three times; Shabbat 'maybe'. Fri: comes for Shabbat after all ('just me'); 'Shir' lights up her phone during the blessing; after dinner a call on the stairs, red eyes, 'plumbers, the landlord, whatever'; the armchair again. Ishai keeps 'no questions'. Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19: the toaster refund; 'I want to be paid for what I already did'. Yael let slip Noa paid cash. Homework (a no to someone he likes) used on Noa's plumbers, then on Gadi's Shabbat 'tiny thing'. Lesson 4 Thu Nov 26, the last one Noa paid for.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Thu: bronchitis; cats every morning; at midnight she came for two eggs: Eli sent a yellow heart, 'far is a choice'. Fri: Moti brings his wife's chicken; she wants the video call working on her phone 'in case someone far calls'; Moti: 'not yet'. Next: Ishai quietly messages Eli (week 3).
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Tue: no proverb, a lawyer's envelope. Thu: 'the proverbs are finished, I have a calculator'; 'Gadi is a cloud'. Next: Ishai asks properly (week 3); the first date starts at his kiosk Saturday.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Wed: chapter thirteen, the coat for a cold city; 'up north'. Fri: chapter fourteen, 'the barista practises the names of streets she has never walked'; asks Ishai if he knows streets up north. Ishai still doesn't recognise himself ('the man in your book sounds like a pushover').
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Thu night out at The Black Candle: fettuccine at Ishai's, then beers; Noa is dodging his messages; he bet Ishai fifty that 'she' (Dana) is moving to Eilat. Next: showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat: one true sentence for the photo; Dana sat on his bench Thursday 'looking at her phone like it was the sea... not this sea'. 1971: 'I stayed.'

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 19: Boaz invited Ishai at Avi's (50 to buy in, small notes, don't touch Yossi's cap); Fri: Moti 'counts the pizza slices'. First night Mon Nov 23 (engine). After it: Yossi asks Ishai to lend him 200.
arcs.secret: Yossi is broke: the lucky cap hasn't paid in months, and he owes money at the depot.

beats.goal: Late morning after his night out, Ishai finally feeds Mrs. Levi's cats on the landing, two hours late; Ben-Gurion complains. Moti comes up the stairs with a pot of his wife's Shabbat chicken for Mrs. Levi. Moti says she asked him to make the video call work on her phone, 'in case someone far calls'; Ishai asks if Eli is coming, Moti says 'not yet' and changes the subject. Moti has heard from Boaz about poker and about 'the barista' tomorrow: the whole building knows.
beats.teaser: Ben-Gurion waited two hours for breakfast. Moti has questions.
beats.forceText: Ishai feeds Mrs. Levi's cats late; Moti brings her Shabbat chicken and won't say whether Eli is coming.

forceLines.say: She asked me to fix the video call. In case someone far calls.

forceCommentary.say: Two hours late with the cat food. Ben-Gurion has filed a complaint.
Moti knows about the date. The building has better wifi than Ishai.

moments.text: Ishai, hair still flat from the pillow, shakes dry food into the dish on the landing; Ben-Gurion yowls at him. Moti comes up the stairs carrying a covered pot with both hands.

lines.say: Ten past eleven. The cat has been complaining since nine.
I know. I know. I was out late.
Out. On a Thursday. Write it down, somebody.
The Black Candle. Tomer. One beer.
One beer. And the eyes of three.
What's in the pot?
My wife's chicken. For Shabbat. Mrs. Levi won't cook like this.
How is she this morning?
Coughing like a bus. But she sent me on an errand.
An errand? From bed?
She wants the video call to work on her phone.
The video call. She hates video calls.
'In case someone far calls.' Her words.
Someone far. Eli?
Who knows who. I'm the committee, not the post office.
Is he coming? For the bronchitis?
Not yet.
Not yet is not no.

commentary.say: Ten past eleven. Ben-Gurion has started drafting a complaint to the committee.
'Not yet.' Moti said two words and both of them were hiding something.

moments.text: Moti balances the pot on the railing and looks Ishai up and down. Ben-Gurion finishes eating and sits on Ishai's shoe.

lines.say: So. Monday. Boaz tells me you're playing.
Fifty to buy in. Small notes.
I count everything. Even the pizza slices.
I'll take one slice. Exactly one.
Good. And tomorrow, the barista.
How do you know about tomorrow?
Boaz. Avi. The cat. Everybody.
It's a walk. And a film.
A film on Saturday night. Very serious.
It's a horror film. That's not serious.
Horror is very serious. She'll hold your arm.
That's what Noa said.
Noa. The one who sleeps on your couch?
Plumbers. At her place.
Plumbers. Hm. In this building we have one plumber, and he's me.
Go. Her chicken is getting cold.

commentary.say: The whole building is coming on this date. Bring popcorn for the committee.
'In this building the plumber is me.' Moti, the only honest man on Herzl Street.

update.memory: Ishai fed the cats two hours late, out Thursday night. Mrs. Levi wants the video call working. He asked about Eli; I said not yet.

beats.goal: Friday rush before Shabbat at Cafe Nahat. Dana makes Ishai's coffee and draws the basil leaf, smaller than usual. They fix tomorrow: 18:30 at Avi's, a walk, then the 21:00 film. He asks if it's bad; she says she'll tell him before the film, 'or after, depends how scary it is'. Her phone buzzes with a 04 number; she turns it face down again. Then Lior at his table reads one sentence from chapter fourteen ('the barista practises the names of streets she has never walked') and looks at Ishai too long; Ishai doesn't get it.
beats.teaser: Tomorrow's date gets a time, and Dana's phone rings again
beats.forceText: At Cafe Nahat Dana and Ishai fix tomorrow, 18:30 at Avi's; her phone buzzes and she turns it face down.

forceLines.say: Eighteen thirty. Avi's. Then the film.
And the thing you have to tell me?

forceCommentary.say: A face-down phone. Again. Honey, the table knows more than he does.
The leaf is smaller today. I'm a host, not a botanist, but that's a sign.

moments.text: Cafe Nahat is full: Friday challahs in paper bags, a queue to the door. Dana works the machine fast, sees Ishai and starts his cup without asking.

lines.say: Usual. Don't say anything, the queue is watching.
I wasn't going to say anything.
You were going to say sorry for the queue.
...I was. A little.
Here. Leaf.
It's smaller than usual.
It's Friday. Everything is smaller. Even the leaf.
So. Tomorrow.
Tomorrow. After Shabbat. What time does it end?
Seventeen seventeen. I checked twice.
Of course you did. Eighteen thirty, Avi's?
Eighteen thirty. Then a walk. Then the film.
A horror film. You picked a horror film.
I didn't pick it. It's what's on.
Good answer. Nobody gets blamed.
Your call yesterday. The thing you have to tell me...

commentary.say: A smaller leaf. Oren, write that down. I'm not saying it means something. It means something.
Seventeen seventeen. He checked twice. That's the most romantic thing he's ever said.

moments.text: Dana wipes the steam wand and doesn't look up. Her phone, by the till, lights up with a number starting 04; she turns it face down with one finger.

lines.say: Before the film. Or after. Depends how scary it is.
Is it bad? You said maybe.
I said nothing bad. Maybe.
Those are two very different sentences.
Your phone's ringing. No. Mine.
You're not answering.
It's Friday. Everybody can wait until Sunday.
Everybody except the queue.
Except the queue. Go sit. Drink your leaf.
Dana. I'm glad. About tomorrow.
Me too. Don't say it twice, it'll wear out.
Okay. Once. Done.
Shabbat shalom, Ishai.
Shabbat shalom. Eighteen thirty.

commentary.say: Zero-four. That's the north. I'm just reading the screen, I'm not saying anything.
'Don't say it twice, it'll wear out.' She's terrified. I love her.

update.memory: Friday rush. Fixed tomorrow: 18:30 at Avi's, walk, film. Told him before the film, or after. The 04 number again; turned it over.

moments.text: Ishai sits at the next table to Lior, who has his laptop open and three empty cups. Lior reads aloud from the screen without being asked.

lines.say: Chapter fourteen. Want one sentence? Just one.
Just one. I have a cat schedule.
'The barista practises the names of streets she has never walked.'
That's nice. Sad. Which streets?
That's chapter fifteen.
You always stop at the good part.
That's how chapters work. Do you know any streets up north?
Up north? Why would I?
No reason. Research.
You keep saying research and looking at the counter.
I look at the counter because the coffee is there.
Your cups are empty, Lior.
Exactly. Hope. Bring me one back, the man in my book would.
The man in your book sounds like a pushover.
He is. Everybody likes him anyway.

commentary.say: Lior is writing the whole show into that laptop and Ishai is reviewing it like a stranger.
'Everybody likes him anyway.' I'd buy that book. Out of pity.

update.memory: Read Ishai one sentence of chapter fourteen, the barista and the streets up north. He asked why north. I said research. He still doesn't see it.

beats.goal: Shabbat comes in at 16:18. Alone first, Ishai gets Gadi's Friday text: Shabbat shalom, Sunday 'we sit with everything', and a 'tiny thing' for Ruti's dreidel. Ishai reads it out loud and answers nothing until Sunday. Then Noa arrives after all, with a challah and wine and too much energy ('no questions, you promised'). They light the candles together; as he says the blessing, her phone on the counter lights up: 'Shir'. She turns it face down. He sees it and says nothing.
beats.teaser: Will Noa come for Shabbat after her 'maybe'?
beats.forceText: Noa comes for Shabbat after all; they light the candles, and Shir's name lights up her phone. She turns it over.

forceLines.say: No questions. You promised. Shabbat shalom, Ishush.

forceCommentary.say: 'Shir' on the screen during the blessing. She flipped it faster than a pita.
He saw it. He kept his promise. Painful to watch.

moments.text: The flat smells of soap; two white candles wait on the counter by Moshe. His phone buzzes: Gadi. Ishai reads it out loud to Falafel.

message.say: Shabbat shalom my pixel! Sunday we sit with EVERYTHING. Tiny thing for Ruti's dreidel before then? Five minutes for you.

lines.say: 'Sunday we sit with everything.' And a tiny thing. Five minutes.
No. Sunday. Shabbat shalom, Gadi. Nothing else. Send.

commentary.say: 'Five minutes for you.' Gadi measures time in other people's weekends.
He sent a reply with no sorry in it. Somebody frame that phone.

moments.text: A loud knock. Noa comes in with a challah under one arm and a bottle of red in the other, talking before the door closes.

lines.say: Don't say it. I said maybe, and maybe means yes.
Maybe means maybe. I made soup for two anyway.
Because you knew. Challah, from the good bakery.
It's still warm. You ran?
I don't run. I walked with purpose.
Your bags?
Not tonight. Just me. Just Shabbat.
Okay.
Okay? That's it?
No questions. I promised.
Wow. He keeps promises now. Yael is a witch.
Gadi wanted five minutes on Shabbat. I said Sunday.
You said no to Gadi? Out loud?
In writing. It counts more.
Ishush. I'm so proud I could open the wine.
After the candles. Four minutes.

commentary.say: 'Just me. Just Shabbat.' That's the saddest happy sentence I've heard this week.
He kept a promise and said no to Gadi in one minute. Who is this man.

moments.text: They stand at the counter. Ishai strikes a match and lights the two candles, covers his eyes and says the blessing. On the counter behind them Noa's phone lights up: 'Shir'. She turns it face down without looking.

lines.say: Baruch atah... lehadlik ner shel Shabbat.
Amen. Shabbat shalom, Ishush.
Shabbat shalom.
Your hand was shaking with the match.
It always shakes. It's tradition.
Your grandmother's hand didn't shake.
My grandmother lit candles in a war. I light them next to a basil.
Moshe deserves candles too.
Your phone...
Is resting. It's Shabbat for phones too.
Okay.
You looked at it.
I looked at the candles. The phone was behind them.
Good. Keep looking at the candles.
Soup?
Soup. And wine. And tell me everything about tomorrow.

commentary.say: Shir. On the screen. During the blessing. The candles saw it too.
'Keep looking at the candles.' Noa, babe, we're all looking at the phone.

beats.goal: After Shabbat dinner, wine on the counter. Noa coaches him for tomorrow's date: ask Dana a question about HER for once. Her phone buzzes again and again; she takes it out to the stairs and closes the door. Ishai, alone with Falafel, hears her voice low through the door and doesn't follow (his promise). She comes back with red eyes, says 'plumbers, the landlord, whatever', asks for the armchair one more night. He gives her a blanket and asks nothing.
beats.teaser: Noa's phone won't stop buzzing on Shabbat. Ishai promised no questions.
beats.forceText: Noa takes a call on the stairs and comes back with red eyes; Ishai gives her a blanket and asks nothing.

forceLines.say: Plumbers. The landlord. Whatever. Can I have the armchair?
Blanket's on the shelf. No questions.

forceCommentary.say: Red eyes and 'plumbers'. Ishai, ask. Don't ask. I can't take it.
The kindest thing he's done all week, and it's saying nothing.

moments.text: Dinner is done; the candles have burned low. Noa sits cross-legged on the armchair with her wine, Ishai on the edge of the bed, Falafel between them.

lines.say: So. Tomorrow. Rule one: you ask her a question.
I ask questions. I asked her what time.
About HER. Not about time. Not about the film.
Like what?
Like what she wants. Where she sees herself. Anything.
That's a job interview.
It's a person interview. Rule two: no sorry.
What if I step on her foot?
Then sorry. One. Allowed.
And if she tells me something bad?
She said nothing bad.
She said nothing bad, maybe.
Then you listen. You're good at listening. To everyone but you.
That's almost a compliment.
It's a whole compliment. Drink.

commentary.say: Rule one: ask about her. Noa, take your own advice, sweetheart.
'A person interview.' Ishai will bring a printed CV.

moments.text: Noa's phone buzzes on the counter. Then again. Then a third time. She looks at it, puts down her glass and stands up.

lines.say: I have to take this. Outside.
It's Shabbat. And it's cold on the stairs.
Two minutes. Don't look at me like that.
I'm looking at the soup.
Keep looking at the soup.
Take the beanie. It's on the shelf. Hostage released.
...Thanks, Ishush.

commentary.say: Three buzzes on Shabbat. That's not a plumber. Plumbers rest too.
He gave her back the beanie. I'm not crying, the studio is dusty.

moments.text: The door clicks shut. Through it comes Noa's voice, low, then lower. Falafel sits at the door with his ears up. Ishai takes a step toward it, stops, and goes back to the counter.

lines.say: No questions. I said no questions.
Falafel. Come. We're not listening. We're washing plates.

commentary.say: One step to the door and back. That's growth. Or torture. Same thing.
The hascii is listening for both of them.

moments.text: The door opens. Noa comes back in with the beanie pulled low and red eyes, and sits on the armchair without taking off her coat.

lines.say: Plumbers. The landlord. Whatever.
Okay.
Can I have the armchair? One more night.
The blanket's on the shelf. The good one.
The good one. You never give me the good one.
Tonight is a good-one night.
You're not going to ask.
I promised. Tea?
Tea. With honey. Like Mrs. Levi.
Like Mrs. Levi. Coming.
Ishush?
Mm?
Tomorrow, ask her the question. Don't be like me.
Like you how?
Go make the tea.

commentary.say: 'Don't be like me.' Noa just said more in four words than in two weeks.
He made tea instead of asking. In this building that's a love language.

update.memory: Came for Shabbat after all. Shir called three times; I cried on his stairs and said plumbers. He gave me the good blanket and asked nothing.

hook.text: Noa came back from the stairs with red eyes and said 'plumbers'. He promised no questions. Tomorrow Dana tells him something. Who talks first?

previously.text: Dana called: 'can it wait until Saturday, at the cinema?' He cooked fettuccine for Tomer, then a beer bet at the bar. At midnight Mrs. Levi came for eggs: Eli sent a yellow heart.

hosts: Friday. Ishai slept till ten after a Thursday night out. The cats did not.
Ben-Gurion the cat ate at eleven today. He will remember this.
Moti carries a pot of chicken up the stairs like it's a committee document.
Mrs. Levi wants the video call working. Mrs. Levi hates video calls. Think about it.
Tomorrow Ishai has a date. Today the whole building has an opinion.
Cafe Nahat on a Friday: half challah, half queue, one barista.
Dana's phone keeps lighting up. She keeps turning it over. Very calm. Very normal.
Lior is on chapter fourteen. He types faster when Dana walks past.
Gadi says Sunday a lot. Sunday is starting to sound like a place.
Five minutes, says Gadi. Five minutes on a Friday is two hours and an apology.
Shabbat comes in at 16:18. Ishai checked. Twice.
Two candles, one basil, one hascii. That's a Shabbat table.
Noa said maybe. With Noa, maybe has many meanings.
Moshe gets a front-row seat for the candles tonight.
Tomer bet Ishai that someone is moving to Eilat. Tomer bets on everything.
Poker on Monday. Moti counts the pizza slices. Plan accordingly.
Ishai's nap is at one. The man has a schedule tighter than Gadi's excuses.
The market closes at two on Fridays. After that it's flowers and panic.
Somewhere a phone with a 04 number is waiting for someone to pick up.
Every person on this street has a word so nobody asks the next question.
Mrs. Levi's cough has opinions. Loud ones.
Tomorrow: Avi's at 18:30, a walk, and a horror film. Romance, building edition.
Noa gives great advice. To other people.
If Ishai says sorry tomorrow, Noa wants a full report.
A quiet Friday night. Quiet doesn't mean nothing's happening.
The challah is from the good bakery. Noa only brings the good bakery when it matters.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Friday edition. Buy your challah now, the queue is already philosophical.
Weather says clear and mild. Perfect for walking to places you should have gone yesterday.
Traffic on the coast road: everybody going to their mother at the same time.
A listener asks if you can freeze flowers. You can. Don't.
Shabbat comes in at 16:18 in Tel Aviv. Turn off the oven you forgot.
Our Friday request line: songs for people who say 'maybe'.
Reminder from the city: the fountain on Herzl east does not take wishes after 23:00.
Fun fact: the average Friday has three more hugs than a Tuesday. We made that up. Feels true.
Next hour: slow songs for fast kitchens.
If your phone is buzzing, maybe it's us. It isn't. Pick it up anyway.
Shabbat shalom from Radio Herzl. Light something warm.

zelig: Friday the pigeons eat early. They have plans.
A candle is a clock that tells you to sit down.
Everybody leaves on Sunday. Nobody leaves on Friday.
The sea is busy today. I'll come back.
michal: Friday run club, seven sharp. I'll be there in spirit.
Mirror says one more set. Mirror lies.
sivan: Friday pace is a lazy pace. Not mine.
Six kilometres before challah. That's the rule.
lior: Chapter fourteen. Streets she has never walked.
Don't look at the counter. Write.
The man in the book says thank you to the door. Keep that.
kobi: Friday numbers are luckier. Every week I say that.
Seven, eleven, the barista's table number.
One drink before Shabbat. Then one more for the lottery.
Who's the guy in the corner? Ah. The apologiser.

street: ...I told her challah, she bought a bagel, now it's a whole thing...
...no, the bus stops at two on Friday, run...
...my mother says come at five, which means four...
...flowers for both mothers-in-law, same colour, it's diplomacy...
market: ...last call for strawberries, last call, half price for nice people...
...he closes at two but he means one-thirty...
...is this the good tahini or the Friday tahini...
...three kilos of potatoes, my cousin is coming from Haifa...
park: ...he walks the dog, the dog walks him, same thing...
...just ten minutes, then we light candles at my aunt's...
...the duck has a new friend, did you see...
cafe: ...two cappuccinos and a challah, the round one...
...she didn't even look at her phone, that's love or a fight...
...no, Friday is not a work day, I'm here for the croissant...
...my brother moved north and now he talks about the air...

chat.say: Reminder: stair light on floor 1 is fixed. Please don't touch the switch with wet hands.
Who is shouting at nine in the morning? Oh. The cat. Never mind.
Chicken delivered to Apt 3. Signed, the committee and his wife.
Anyone have a spare challah tray? Mine became a poker chip tray.
Does anyone know how to make the camera thing on the phone face the right way?
Apt 3: press the little arrows. Coming up after Shabbat to show you.
Shabbat shalom everyone. Quiet tonight please, the baby sleeps at last.
Shabbat shalom. Ishai, the grey one likes it warm. Tomorrow too.
